places.text: Sixty-odd tombs cut into a single dry valley, most of them painted floor to ceiling.
places.title: The Valley of the Kings

places.text: Karnak took two thousand years to build; Abu Simbel was moved sixty metres to save it.
places.title: Karnak, Luxor, Abu Simbel

places.text: Twenty million people on the Nile, and a Mediterranean city that remembers being Greek.
places.title: Cairo and Alexandria

places.text: The mosques, sabils and madrasas of the medieval city, largely still standing.
places.title: Mamluk Cairo

places.text: Three layers still in daily use, sometimes in the same street in old Cairo.
places.title: Coptic, Islamic, Pharaonic

places.text: Nubian villages above Aswan and Bedouin communities in the Sinai and the Western Desert.
places.title: Nubians and Bedouin

places.text: The moulid processions, and Cairo at iftar when the whole city eats at once.
places.title: Moulids and Ramadan

places.text: Hand-blown glass in Cairo, Egyptian cotton, and papyrus made the way it always was.
places.title: Papyrus, Glass and Cotton

places.text: Families out along the river, tea on the pavement, and the traffic finally slowing.
places.title: The Corniche at Dusk

places.text: The Nile's cataracts at Aswan — rapids rather than falls, and the reason the boats stopped here.
places.title: The First Cataract

places.text: Feluccas under sail at Aswan, and a river that has been the country's main road for millennia.
places.title: The Nile Itself

places.text: Some of the clearest reef diving on earth, an hour's flight from the pyramids.
places.title: The Red Sea

places.text: A green ribbon a few kilometres wide, and sand for a thousand kilometres either side of it.
places.title: The Nile and the Desert

places.text: Two million migrating birds use the Delta and the Red Sea coast as a flyway each year.
places.title: Birds of the Delta

places.text: Not big game — desert fox, gazelle and the silence of the Great Sand Sea.
places.title: The Western Desert

places.text: Mount Sinai and Saint Catherine's, and granite peaks over two thousand metres above the Red Sea.
places.title: Sinai

places.text: Not forest — the Fayoum's palm and olive, and the acacia of Wadi el-Rayan.
places.title: The Fayoum

places.text: Diving the Red Sea, walking the Sinai with Bedouin guides, and crossing the sand sea by vehicle.
places.title: Desert Crossings

places.text: Breakfast is ful and bread; lunch is koshary; both are older than most cuisines.
places.title: Ful, Koshary and Bread

places.text: Short internal flights, boats instead of buses, and a story at every stop.
places.title: Straightforward with Children

places.text: Reef diving at Marsa Alam, feluccas at Aswan, and camels in the Western Desert.
places.title: Dive, Sail, Ride

places.text: Small sailing dahabiyas instead of the big cruisers, and camps in the White Desert.
places.title: Dahabiyas and Desert Camps

places.text: Reef protection on the Red Sea, and oasis agriculture that has managed water for millennia.
places.title: Reef and Oasis

places.text: Desert light at either end of the day is the whole reason to be up early here.
places.title: The Light at Six

places.text: Eight hundred kilometres west, a Berber-speaking oasis with its own language and salt lakes.
places.title: Siwa

places.text: People have been travelling to see this country for two and a half thousand years.
places.title: The Oldest Journey
